text:
Sam R: Heads-up, running a sales POC demo in eu-west-1. Customer saw a flurry of 500/503s during a scripted burst. Call paused. Can support swarm?
Elena P: On it. Quick details: which model/route, qps pattern, and any client-side retries?
Sam R: Route: routes/poc-eu/demo-abc, model rwl-13b-v2, pattern: steady 120 qps for 90s then ramp to 850 qps for 20s. Client has exponential backoff (3 retries).
Theo B: 850 qps for 20s will hit autoscaler cooldowns. Any response headers from failures?
Sam R: Pasted one response: ```HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Date: Wed, 02 Oct 2059 09:22:14 GMT
x-redwood-queue-length: 290
x-redwood-reason: capacity_spill
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "runtime overloaded"
}```
Elena P: Queue length ~290 is high. monitoring-bot, show autoscaler events and recent backoffs in eu-west-1 for that route.
monitoring-bot: [event] autoscaler: scale_up_trigger at 09:22:06 reason=queue_threshold route=poc-eu/demo-abc
monitoring-bot: [event] autoscaler: scale_up_start at 09:22:08 policy=latency_target
monitoring-bot: [event] autoscaler: scale_up_complete at 09:22:33 added_replicas=3
Theo B: Scale finished after the 20s burst ended. Looks like scale latency ~25s + model cold-start time. That explains 503 spikes.
Elena P: Two approaches: (A) reserve headroom for this customer (min_replicas bump / dedicated burstpool) or (B) apply client-side pacing to avoid the hard burst. For a demo they want no behavioral change in model output. Recommend short-term reserve.
Sam R: Customer asked to avoid model variant changes. They're okay with us reserving capacity for the demo window if we can propose pricing.
Theo B: Quick mitigation I can apply now: 1) bump min_replicas for the route by +4; 2) temporarily mark route as high-priority so background jobs yield; 3) enable connection warmup hook to reduce cold starts. Note (3) may need a small runtime flag.
Elena P: Ops-bot, can you apply 1 and 2 and pause large eval jobs in eu-west?
ops-bot: applying config: PATCH /v1/routes/poc-eu/demo-abc { min_replicas: 8 } by Theo B at 09:23:05
ops-bot: applied: route/poc-eu/demo-abc min_replicas=8
ops-bot: paused jobs: eval-batch-large-07 in eu-west by Theo B at 09:23:18
Sam R: Re-ran the scripted burst after changes. Result: queue length peaked ~40, 5xxs reduced to 1 short 502. Customer back on the call.
Elena P: Grab a log bundle for 09:21:50-09:24:00 (runtime + autoscaler + frontdoor). Also need stack traces for 502.
Sam R: Uploaded logs: https://s3.redwood-internal/poc-dumps/2823456789/logs.tar.gz
Theo B: Quick grep shows the 502s are from a worker process OOM during model mmap while warming weights. Two diagnostics: small memory spike + delayed healthcheck pass.
Elena P: So root causes: autoscaler latency + intermittent cold-start OOMs for rwl-13b-v2. Short-term steps done. For long-term: warmup improvements and prefetch memory reservation. I'll file INF-4992 for warmup and MEM-221 for runtime memory management.
Sam R: Customer also asked about an SLA/commit for pilot (headroom guarantee) and security: they need isolation/attestation for enterprise PII. What's the sales/SE play?
Elena P: For enterprise pilots we offer reserved burstpool (monthly commitment) + Private deployment or Dedicated nodes for isolation. Pricing varies; I'll send James in sales a tailored quote. For attestation we can provide KMS integration and SOC artifacts.
Theo B: Also, if they take Dedicated or Private, autoscale is much faster (prewarmed fleet) and cold-starts are rare. Recommend that for production pilots needing burst guarantees.
Sam R: Customer accepted the immediate mitigation and asked for a formal follow-up tomorrow. They want a written plan for preventing 5xxs in demo scenarios plus cost estimate.
Elena P: Action items: - Elena: draft proposal (reserved burstpool + pricing + security checklist) and DM to Sam - Theo: open INF-4992 (warmup perf) and MEM-221 (OOM protection) - Ops: keep min_replicas=8 for the demo window (till 09:45) and then revert to previous baseline
ops-bot: scheduled revert: route/poc-eu/demo-abc min_replicas -> 4 at 09:45 by Theo B
Sam R: Thanks all. Live call resumed and customer completed the demo. Saved the pilot. I'll follow up with their requested times for the next run. :relieved:
